Yeah, I think the best dietary advice is to listen to your body. It knows what you need better than you do. I think overeating is such a big problem in the countries with an industrialized food industry because so many of our foods are nutrient deficient. If you aren't getting the nutrients you need, your body lets you know, but if you misinterpret that hunger and keep eating empty calories it doesn't solve the root of the problem, it just masks the symptoms (parallel to the pharmaceutical industry). If you look at my ethnic background (high latitude Europe), my ancestors had to eat more meat to make up for the lessened availability of plant-based food sources due to environmental constraints (and was one of the groups of humans to develop lactase persistence). I tried to do the whole vegetarian thing once and ended up with a terrible iron deficiency and lost way too much weight. You may say I just wasn't doing vegetarianism right, and there is some truth to that, but I think my body just likes a more protein and fat diet in my diet than people whose ancestors relied heavily on tubers and grains for sustenance. I feel better that way, and it works for me. Overall, humans are omnivorous to the extreme and we have the capacity to make do with a vast array of different foods. What I've found works best is to just have a variety of different foods to chose from so that your body can tell you what you need. Open the fridge, see some kale and decide you want a salad? Awesome, let's get some vit A and K up in here. Want eggs and bacon all of a sudden? Great, sounds like time for some protein and choline. Feel shitty after eating the whole pack of bacon? Moderation is key, as with anything. Learn what works for you. And BTW, cholesterol is necessary for animal cell wall integrity and is a precursor to various hormones and vitamin D, though you can make your own from fatty acids.

Basically, today I did something different. I squatted ATG on low bar and it felt fucking awesome. A bit harder perhaps, but fucking awesome. Now I was wondering if this is bad for me somehow? I mean I kept my core tight and I didn't have any noticeable buttwink. But from what I gathered, you are only supposed to go parallel or a bit below when you low bar squat. Is there a reason why? I tried looking it up online but I couldn't find any valid reason why.

Any input is appreciated. :)

I'm not a professional but I think if you let your knees adapt to the stress gradually you should be fine. If you feel pain or weakness in your knee joints, just stop stressing them for a while and let them recover. Don't push them to hard right away.

People use to think squats were screwing up knees, but that came from a study done on paratroopers in the military.

Oh awesome, thank you! So far, so good with my knees but I'll definitely follow your advice if something comes up.

Also, you are completely right. Squats (when done properly) are actually good for the knees as they strengthen the muscles around them. I'm not sure about that study, but from what I read half squats are especially detrimental to the knees.
True! I'm in my 40's and my knees used to get sore every once in a while (nothing serious, just annoying). Ever since I started squatting heavy my knees have been great. They never get sore anymore.

There is no reason not to. I regularly squat fairly ATG (low bar) and the issue of buttwink is generally not considered too important.

Your knees won't explode, don't worry.
